builder_plan.scenario: Profiling shows attention computation is a bottleneck in your self-hosted service.
builder_plan.change: Check the supported GPU, tensor shapes, and precision, then replace only the relevant kernel.
builder_plan.baseline: The existing kernel inside the same complete serving pipeline.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Numerical differences, end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory at realistic shapes.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Tucker Bottleneck Attention for Multi-Dimensional Sequence Modeling
summary: TuBA replaces full self-attention over long multidimensional token sequences (video frames, weather grids) with attention performed on compact low-rank Tucker cores, projecting hidden tensors down, mixing globally in the compressed space, and writing updates back. The cost is added architectural complexity: projection into and out of Tucker cores, a specialized autoregressive variant combining intra-core bidirectional and inter-core causal attention, and a rank hyperparameter that must be tuned per task. It can fail if the data lacks exploitable low-rank tensor structure, if the chosen core rank is too small and bottlenecks information flow, and its demonstrated gains are confined to video prediction and weather forecasting, with no evidence for language or general sequence workloads.
rationale: The claimed compute and error reductions are substantial and compatible with a single 24 GB GPU, but the method is validated only on multidimensional scientific/vision tasks and requires non-trivial reimplementation, so workload-specific validation on a small pilot is warranted before adoption.
technique: Tucker bottleneck attention for multidimensional sequences

claims.statement: TuBA replaces full self-attention over long multidimensional token sequences (video frames, weather grids) with attention performed on compact low-rank Tucker cores, projecting hidden tensors down, mixing globally in the compressed space, and writing updates back. The cost is added architectural complexity: projection into and out of Tucker cores, a specialized autoregressive variant combining intra-core bidirectional and inter-core causal attention, and a rank hyperparameter that must be tuned per task. It can fail if the data lacks exploitable low-rank tensor structure, if the chosen core rank is too small and bottlenecks information flow, and its demonstrated gains are confined to video prediction and weather forecasting, with no evidence for language or general sequence workloads.

Up to 4.27x speedup over standard self-attention, with computation reduced by up to 66.6% (video prediction) and 85.1% (autoregressive weather forecasting), while simultaneously reducing error by up to 24.7% and 37.1% respectively.
